Ever pasted the right thing into the wrong window? It may not be lost focus.
Neuroscientist Cheng Xue assumed it was. So his Chicago team built a game.
Two stripe patterns change at once. Only one change counts, and the rule secretly flips.
Over two hundred people played. So did two monkeys, with their neurons recorded.
When the rule was unclear, the mistakes weren't random. They followed a pattern.
After a miss, people remembered the very detail they should have ignored.
In the monkeys, the signals for the two features began to overlap.
So a slip while juggling tasks may be crosstalk, not weak willpower. Leave a pause between tasks.
Latoon. Voyaging the unseen. Follow for more.
